question.text: As per SEBI Circular dated October 22, 2020, for processing an AIF registration application and scheme launch, external members of the proposed Investment Committee (for investment decisions) must be:

answer.text: Foreign-qualified chartered financial analysts with minimum 10 years experience
Independent directors as per the Companies Act, 2013 definition
Resident Indian citizens; if they are non-resident Indian citizens, the application is processed only after receiving due clarifications from the Government and RBI
Holders of SEBI Investment Adviser certification only

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Ch 11.7.3 and SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/IMD/DF6/CIR/P/2020/209 dated October 22, 2020, external IC members must be resident Indian citizens. If the external members are non-resident Indian citizens, the application is processed only after receiving due clarifications from the Government and RBI. **The Trap:** CFA qualification and Companies Act independent-director definition are not imposed. Option D narrows certification requirements in a way the circular does not. **Cross-Exam Context:** This residency rule is a specific XIX-C governance point not covered at the same granularity in XIX-A/B. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** If you want a global advisor on the IC, structure them as an Advisory Board member (observer), not a voting IC member — the Advisory Board does not attract the residency requirement.
